panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E histology demonstrating the characteristic wedge-shaped superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate of PLEVA, along with spongiotic vesiculation and reticular degeneration. B: Higher-power H&E histology showing basal layer vacuolization (interface change), lymphocytic exocytosis, and dermal red blood cell extravasation—all characteristic histological features of PLEVA. C: Immunohistochemistry confirming the lymphocytic infiltrate is composed of CD3-positive T cells, supporting the diagnosis of PLEVA. D: Immunohistochemistry demonstrating intraepidermal CD30-positive cells, a recognized feature in some PLEVA biopsies.
